newsitem.title: USA: Low ham stocks seen boosting CME hog prices.
newsitem.headline: Low ham stocks seen boosting CME hog prices.

text.p: Sharply lower than year ago ham stocks reported in Friday's USDA monthly cold storage report are expected to spark a further rally in CME hog futures next week, livestock analysts said.

"I expect at some point here in the next 40 to 50 days that we are going to see packers chasing after hogs to get the hams," said Dale Benson, vice president and senior livestock analyst for Dean Witter.
Analyst expectations are for hog futures to trade 0.200 to 0.300 cent per lb higher Monday.

USDA reported bone-in ham stocks at 53.3 million lbs, only 66 percent of last year's frozen stocks of 93.5 million lbs. Boneless ham stocks were 2.0 million lbs under last year and canned hams 6.5 million lb below last year.
Benson expects commodity ham prices, currently at $84 per cwt, to go up to $105 to $110 by the Thanksgiving holiday. "There's just not enough hams to go around," he said.

Analysts ranged from neutral to somewhat bullish for pork belly futures after the storage report showed frozen belly stocks at 18.9 million lbs. Pork bellies could be 0.100 to 1.000 cents higher Monday based on the report, they said.
"That (belly number) allows the longs in the (futures) market to breathe a sigh of relief," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.

Levitt noted that traders voiced concern that some bellies may be found in storage after the low number reported in the storage report last month. But belly stocks remained low compared to most years and this should support belly futures.
Beef (hamburger) stocks were up from last month but remained 40 million lbs under year ago levels at 304.9 million lbs. Five or six months of good beef demand has kept beef stocks down.
However, continued rising frozen poultry supplies may temper any expected gains in CME meat contracts. Poultry stocks totaled 1,322.9 million lbs, up from 1,160.7 million lbs last year.
